models.benchmark_scope: transferable organic force field trained for neutral organic chemistry
models.why_relevant: MACE-OFF is a real chemistry-domain foundation model for organics, so it is a credible prior for molecular geometry tasks.
models.caution: Its published scope does not by itself prove transition-state stability, proton-shuttle fidelity, or sulfur transferability for Maillard chemistry.
source_notes: MACE README describes MACE-OFF23 as a transferable organic force field released for organic chemistry and suitable as a starting point for fine-tuning.
The same README distinguishes materials-focused MACE-MP from chemistry-focused molecular models.

models.benchmark_scope: materials foundation model trained on bulk crystal trajectories
models.why_relevant: It remains worth tracking only because our internal geometry benchmark already found bounded utility for offline preoptimization.
models.caution: External evidence positions MACE-MP as a materials model, not as a chemistry-first molecular model for reaction barriers.
source_notes: MACE README lists MACE-MP as a Materials Project force field trained on bulk crystals and separate from molecular checkpoints.

models.benchmark_scope: molecular foundation model with charge/spin embedding and very good molecular accuracy
models.why_relevant: Among current MACE families, OMOL is the closest public molecular foundation candidate to our chemistry-first needs.
models.caution: The published molecular accuracy claim still does not substitute for local checks on Maillard TS seeds, proton transfer, and sulfur chemistry.
source_notes: MACE README lists MACE-OMOL-0 as a molecular checkpoint with charge/spin embedding and very good molecular accuracy.

models.benchmark_scope: molecular neural potential for neutral and charged organic or elemental-organic systems with forces and Hessians
models.why_relevant: AIMNet2 already exposes the interfaces and molecular charge handling that make it a serious chemistry-first TS seeding candidate for our workflow.
models.caution: External molecular benchmarks still do not establish robustness on our decisive failure modes: proton shuttles, sulfur chemistry, and benchmark-visible barrier ordering.
source_notes: AIMNet2 README states that the calculator targets neutral, charged, organic, and elemental-organic systems and supports ASE and PySisyphus interfaces.
The same README documents optional forces, stress, and Hessian evaluation plus long-range Coulomb options for large systems.

models.benchmark_scope: molecular Orb checkpoint trained on OMol25 high-accuracy DFT calculations with explicit charge and spin inputs
models.why_relevant: OrbMol is now a real molecular branch rather than a pure materials model, making it legitimate to shortlist for offline TS and geometry acceleration.
models.caution: Its public documentation highlights broad molecular coverage, not validated Maillard reaction pathways or TS-specific barrier fidelity.
source_notes: Orb repo documents August 2025 OrbMol release trained on OMol25 with over 100M omegaB97M-V/def2-TZVPD molecular calculations.
The same repo states that OrbMol accepts explicit total charge and spin multiplicity.

models.why_relevant: It remains a useful negative control because strong materials branding can otherwise be mistaken for chemistry-domain relevance.
models.caution: External positioning is centered on advanced materials rather than reaction-level molecular organic chemistry.
source_notes: Orbital research pages position Orb primarily as a leading AI model for advanced materials.
